exposure to moderate or strong hyposaline solutions resulted in three response patterns in IL: a decrease, a biphaic effect, and a increase; exposure to strong hyposaline solution resulted only in an increase in IT; and exposure to either moderate of strong hyposalina solution resulted only in increases IL and IT in intact pituitay cells (perforatd patch method).

exposure of rat anterior pituitaries cells to hyposmolarity (moderate or strong) resulted in a differential and voltage-independent increase in both L-type (IL), and T-type (I T) voltage-gated calcium currents.
exposure to hyposmotic solutions (decrease in extracellular osmotic concentration) can directly increase voltage-gated calcium channels currents in anterior pituitary cell.

the role of calcium in the regulation of cell function.
the mechanisms underlying the hyposmotic activation of hormone secretion from anterior pituitary.
the mechanisms by which changes in extracellular osmotic pressure affect the electrical properties of cells.
